## Security Review

- Server-side validation remains in the existing shared Laravel password rule. No alternate authentication path was added.
- Framework password hashing and storage remain unchanged. Reset tests continue to verify `Hash::check`, account-state preservation, database-session invalidation, and omission of tokens and passwords from activity metadata.
- Production-only `uncompromised()` remains enabled in `AppServiceProvider.php`.
- No route, API, private-file, access-state, verification, rate-limit, queue, scheduler, or deployment carrier changed.
- The screenshot contains synthetic `Synthetic Test User` and `matic-synthetic@example.test` data only; password fields were cleared. No password, token, cookie, private key, or real participant data is present.
- R-19 (Lowering password requirements may increase weak-password compromise risk or conflict with security acceptance) remains Open. Local enforcement evidence does not quantify production compromise risk or establish production security acceptance.
